title: Mythical Animals of the Forbidden City
synopsis: Which auspicious animals live in Beijing’s Forbidden City?

fullText.simplified:
故宫神兽谈

    不是每一种动物都能在600多年的紫禁城里得到一席之地的，今天我们就来说说这些故宫里的小神兽。
    故宫建筑不同方位里的祥禽瑞兽，不仅镇宅化煞、驱邪迎祥，同时它们也用几百年来的同一个姿势，执着地期盼江山牢固、国泰民安。
    故宫内的铜狮很多，个头最大、造型最精美的要数太和殿门前的一对。右边雄狮右前爪下有一个缠绕绶带的绣球，象征着统一世界；左边雌狮左前爪下逗弄幼崽，寓意子孙昌盛。据说这对铜狮的头上一共有45个发髻，暗示九五之尊。最有意思的是乾清门前的两只耷拉着耳朵的狮子，因为乾清门是通向皇帝妻子们住的地方，摆放两只耷拉耳朵的狮子正是想告诉皇帝的妻子们：不该听的别瞎打听。
    除了铜狮以外，还有铜鹤、铜龟、铜象等，寓意是“长寿”和“富贵吉祥”。
    故宫的房顶上也有很多神兽。比如“斗牛”、“天马”、“海马”等，这些神兽都是吉祥、除祸灭灾和皇权的象征。比如，太和殿屋顶上，就排列坐着10个小神兽，象征着皇权的至高无上。
    如果你对中国建筑文化感兴趣，一定要去故宫看看这些可爱的神兽呀！
fullText.traditional:
故宮神獸談

    不是每一種動物都能在600多年的紫禁城裡得到一席之地的，今天我們就來說說這些故宮裡的小神獸。
    故宮建築不同方位裡的祥禽瑞獸，不僅鎮宅化煞、驅邪迎祥，同時它們也用幾百年來的同一個姿勢，執著地期盼江山牢固、國泰民安。
    故宮內的銅獅很多，個頭最大、造型最精美的要數太和殿門前的一對。右邊雄獅右前爪下有一個纏繞綬帶的繡球，象徵著統一世界；左邊雌獅左前爪下逗弄幼崽，寓意子孫昌盛。據說這對銅獅的頭上一共有45個髮髻，暗示九五之尊。最有意思的是乾清門前的兩隻耷拉著耳朵的獅子，因為乾清門是通向皇帝妻子們住的地方，擺放兩隻耷拉耳朵的獅子正是想告訴皇帝的妻子們：不該聽的別瞎打聽。
    除了銅獅以外，還有銅鶴、銅龜、銅象等，寓意是“長壽”和“富貴吉祥”。
    故宮的房頂上也有很多神獸。比如“鬥牛”、“天馬”、“海馬”等，這些神獸都是吉祥、除禍滅災和皇權的象徵。比如，太和殿屋頂上，就排列坐著10個小神獸，象徵著皇權的至高無上。
    如果你對中國建築文化感興趣，一定要去故宮看看這些可愛的神獸呀！

raw.synopsis: Which auspicious animals live in Beijing’s Forbidden City?
sentence_translations: Mythical Animals of the Forbidden City
Not every kind of animal can get a place in the Forbidden City, which has a history of more than 600 years.
Today, we will talk about the small mythical animals in the Forbidden City.
The auspicious birds and animals located in different parts of the Forbidden City ..
.. not only protect the residence, driving away evil spirits and bringing good fortune, ..
.. they’ve also maintained the same position for hundreds of years, ..
.. persistently hoping for a strong country and peace and prosperity.
There are many bronze lions in the Forbidden City.
The pair in front of the Hall of Supreme Harmony have the biggest heads and are the most exquisite.
The male lion on the right has an embroidered ball wrapped around by a ribbon under his right front paw, ..
.. which symbolizes a unified world.
The female lion on the left is playing with her cubs with her left front paw, representing the prosperity of offspring.
It is said that there are a total of 45 lumps on the two bronze lions’ heads, referring to the imperial throne.
The two lions with drooping ears in front of the Gate of Heavenly Purity are the most interesting ones, ..
.. because the Gate of Heavenly Purity leads to the place where the emperor’s wives lived.
The two lions with drooping ears are there to tell the emperor’s wives, ..
.. don’t foolishly ask about things you’re not meant to hear.
Other than bronze lions, there is also a bronze crane, a bronze turtle, and a bronze elephant, etc., ..
.. meaning “longevity” and “wealth and good fortune”.
There are also many mythical animals on the roof of the Forbidden City.
For example, a “bull”, “heavenly horse”, and “sea horse”, etc.
These mythical animals are symbols of auspiciousness, preventing disasters, and imperial power.
For example, on the roof of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, there are 10 small mythical animals sitting in a row, ..
.. symbolizing the supremacy of imperial power.
If you’re interested in the culture of Chinese architecture, ..
.. you must go to the Forbidden City to see these adorable mythical animals!
